source: QA profile interop assemblies decompiled at %TEMP%\covtrigb\ilspy (Modules-ASM, SNet_ASM, GlobalFramework-ASM); member kinds read from the IL2CPP wrappers, call edges and RVA only where a method body was readable
verifiedBy: InteropCheck build (temporary, %TEMP%\nllevel\interopcheck): LevelEventObservation.cs, LevelEventActions.cs and LevelEventHooks.cs compiled against the real interop assemblies with a session shim; 0 errors. Every member named below is resolved by that build.
LevelEventFacts (ForgeMap/tests/LevelEventFacts): 19 cases over the game-independent contract and module, all green.

rows.memberKind: public static void, IL2CPP wrapper (native token 1006727xx); the game's own "the expedition is running now" entry
rows.derivation: the `map` reference is the active expedition's own identity: `Global.RundownIdToLoad` + `RundownManager.GetActiveExpeditionData().tier/.expeditionIndex`, formatted by MapLevelReference — the same string the `level` attachment matcher compares (evidence/level-identity.json)
rows.authority: host only: the entry runs on the master; a client's copy would be a second publisher of a session fact
rows.clients: no replication needed beyond the fact itself: every client knows its own level identity
rows.unverified: whether the game calls this entry once per level or once per local player session was not read from the method body; the row's own publication is idempotent per world, so a second call publishes nothing

rows.memberKind: public virtual void OnStartInChain on WardenObjective; public static pWardenObjectiveState CurrentState { get; } and public byte GetChainIndexForLayer(LG_LayerType) on pWardenObjectiveState
rows.derivation: a reactor objective's waves are its own event chain (vanilla `ReactorWaves[].Events`, 171 entries across ReactorWaves[0..7]); the chain index the objective machine already reports is therefore the wave, and the row publishes the new index with the previous one
rows.unverified: the exact name of a reactor objective's data block type was not read; the row does not depend on it, because it reads the chain index rather than the objective's type

rows.memberKind: public virtual void (override) on WO_HSUFindTakeSample : WardenObjective; the component also carries `LG_HSU m_hsu`
rows.derivation: the class is the objective component the vanilla `ActivateHSU_Events` list (15 entries) belongs to, so the transition the row reports is the same one the vanilla mount fires on; the container reference is the HSU's own `m_serialNumber`/`m_itemKey`, left out when the component carries neither
rows.authority: host only; both the objective item and the activator are host state
rows.unverified: the exact serial-number identity of the linked item object was not read back from LG_HSUActivator_Core; the row publishes the activator's own two naming members instead of inventing a map-object address for it

rows.memberKind: public void on CheckpointManager (an SNet_StateReplicatorProvider); `CheckpointManager.IsReloadingCheckpoint` and `CheckpointManager.Current` are public static
rows.derivation: this is the entry the game calls once the reloaded world is in place, so the row fires after the state is back rather than when the recall was requested
rows.clients: the host's own suspension policy for the recall is a separate batch's (nl-vars); this row only publishes the fact
rows.unverified: whether this entry runs before or after the reloaded level's own start was not read from the method body; a plan that needs both orders should mount on both rows

rows.memberKind: public static void; the same class also declares the `OnLocalPlayerEnterZoneCallback` event pair and `OnLocalPlayerEnterNewLayerType(LG_LayerType)`
rows.derivation: the address is computed from the zone's own members — `LG_Zone.m_dimensionIndex`, `LG_Zone.m_layer.m_type` (LG_LayerType) and `LG_Zone.IDinLayer` — so it is the same three-layer address `ZoneIndex` resolves for every other level-scope row
rows.authority: host only: the fact is published once per world per player/zone pair, and a client-side copy would double the row
rows.vanillaNote: the vanilla layout's `Zones[].EventsOnZoneEnter` lists are empty in the shipped data, which is why this path was not exercised by any vanilla objective; the compile-time evidence is the member itself, and the runtime behaviour needs one in-game check
rows.unverified: whether this entry fires for every player or only for the local one was not read from the method body; the row's own state key is per player, so a local-only call would publish for the local player only

rows.nativeEntry: LG_DimensionPortal.OnWarp(PlayerAgent warpOwner, AIG_CourseNode fromCourseNode, AIG_CourseNode toCourseNode, AIG_INode toNode)
rows.memberKind: public virtual void on LG_DimensionPortal (an SNet_StateReplicatorProvider with pDimensionPortalState/pDimensionPortalInteraction)
rows.derivation: the destination is the portal's own `m_targetDimension`; the portal's identity is its `m_serialNumber`; the "from" dimension is `fromCourseNode.m_dimension.DimensionIndex`, which is the dimension of the node the player left
rows.vanillaNote: the vanilla mount point is `Zones[].EventsOnPortalWarp` (4 entries); the portal also carries its own `WardenObjectiveEventData m_portalEventData`
rows.unverified: whether OnWarp runs once per player moved or once per portal activation was not read from the method body; the fact's state key is the portal and the destination, so a second player arriving at the same destination publishes nothing new

rows.nativeEntry: WorldEventManager.ExecuteEvent(WardenObjectiveEventData eData, float currentDuration = 0f) with the struct's own `Type`
rows.memberKind: public static void on WorldEventManager (also ExecuteEvent_Internal, ExecuteEvents, DoExcecuteEvent IEnumerator, CheckAndExecuteEventsOnTrigger)
rows.catalogShape: the website's row declares an `objectives` resource input, a `seconds` number input, the structural `operation` enum and a result with a `seconds` field. The resource input is declared because the framework requires an action's recipient port; the handler refuses a plan that supplies one, exactly as the objective action rows already do, and the row is therefore a session-wide event.
rows.authority: host only: the executor runs on the master and the event struct's replicated fields carry the change
rows.unverified: ResetTimer is defined in the enum but appears in none of the shipped objective data (the vanilla `AddToTimer` use is 12 entries in R8_E2), so its exact effect on a countdown is a confirmed-in-game item

rows.nativeEntry: WorldEventManager.ExecuteEvent with the struct's own `Type`; the struct's `DimensionIndex` and `ClearDimension` carry the parameters
rows.authority: host only: LG_DimensionPortal is an SNet_StateReplicatorProvider and the player dimension has its own replicator (pPlayerDimensionChange)
rows.derivation: the catalog's `mode` + `clear` parameter pair maps onto the three members one for one; `clear` is the struct's own field, which vanilla `DimensionWarpTeam` sets in 14 of its 32 uses
rows.unverified: what `ClearDimension` actually removes from a dimension was not read from the method body; the row therefore claims only that the dimension is cleared, not which objects disappear

rows.relatedMembers: WardenObjectiveManager also exposes ForceCompleteObjective(LG_LayerType), ForceCompleteObjectiveAll(LG_LayerType), OnWinConditionSolved(LG_LayerType, bool forceComplete), MasterSetWinOnDeath(), GetWinOnDeath() — the objective action rows already use the first two
rows.unverified: whether ForceInstantWin ends the expedition immediately or arms the objective's own completion check was not read from the method body
